summary: Buffered Responses API tool-call round trips replace the single-turn text-only response-mode conversion. Full conversation history with tools tool_use and tool_result maps to ordered Responses function_call and function_call_output items. Upstream function_call output items are converted to Anthropic tool_use blocks with strict argument validation and correct stop reason tool_use when a valid call is emitted. The proxy still forces stream false for response mode. Implementation in server.py _anthropic_to_response and _response_to_anthropic with 198 tests passing including a live apinebula-codex E2E.

Chat-mode streaming requests from Claude Code were failing to execute commands because _stream_chat_sse_to_anthropic detected OpenAI delta.tool_calls but only set tool_calls_seen = True without emitting any Anthropic tool_use SSE events, then degraded finish_reason: tool_calls to stop_reason: null. The fix added full streaming tool-call delta conversion: per-index tool state keyed by validated upstream OpenAI tool index, contiguous monotonic Anthropic block indices shared with thinking/text, metadata buffering with capped pending fragments (64 KB per tool, 32 tracked indexes, 32 concurrent open blocks), isinstance-guarded field access, intra-frame ordering (deltas before finish), ascending-index close order, and dict-only json.loads validation at close. Conservative degradation rules: stop_reason: tool_use is claimed only when all started tools are parseable with no fragments dropped, no overflow, and no frame-dropped+emitted conflict; all other cases degrade to null. A coalesced chat_sse_tool_degradation trace event (metadata-only, no tool names/IDs/fragments) fires once per affected stream. A review found 5 findings (2 Warning, 3 Suggestion) all fixed: empty tool_calls: [] sentinel no longer inflates tool_calls_seen, mixed parseable+unparseable parallel finish degrades to null, non-dict JSON parses count as unparseable, start-failure branch clears pending fragments, and the frame_dropped guard plus tool_calls: [] sentinel are tested. 22 new permanent tests added, 1 degradation-locking test replaced. Full suite: 180/180 passed, 0 failed. Files: src/claude_retry_proxy/server.py, tests/test_claude_proxy.py. CLAUDE.md and README.md updated to remove the streaming-tool-call-deltas deferred issue.

Fixed the chat-mode thinking/reasoning round-trip in the proxy so that DeepSeek V4 and similar reasoning models work correctly in multi-turn conversations. Previously thinking blocks were stripped from assistant messages in the request transform and reasoning_content was silently dropped in the response transform, causing the upstream to reject multi-turn requests with reasoning_content must be passed back errors. Three fix locations in server.py: _transform_anthropic_messages_to_chat converts thinking blocks to reasoning_content on assistant messages (with last-wins semantics for multiple thinking blocks, redacted_thinking with non-empty data converted to a placeholder with a redacted_thinking_passthrough trace event, real thinking text wins over placeholder); _chat_to_anthropic converts reasoning_content or reasoning for vLLM compat to a thinking content block with signature empty string inserted first in the content array; _stream_chat_sse_to_anthropic handles reasoning and reasoning_content deltas with proper block-index management using deferred content_block_start, monotonic block_index counter, current_block_type tracking, and terminal close of open blocks at their numeric indices. One Plan Gap was found and fixed: open_blocks stored block type strings instead of numeric block_index, causing terminal-path content_block_stop events to carry string indices. The reference implementation was OA2A local-openai2anthropic converter.py and streaming handler.py. 8 permanent tests added, 5 existing tests updated, 159 total tests pass. CLAUDE.md and README.md updated to reflect the behavioral change thinking blocks converted, not stripped. Two deferred issues remain unresolved: streaming tool call deltas and image content blocks.

Fixed the chat-mode request transform in the proxy's Anthropic-to-Chat conversion. Previously _anthropic_to_chat passed Anthropic messages through unchanged to the OpenAI Chat Completions API, causing 400 errors from third-party providers. Three new transform functions were added: _transform_anthropic_messages_to_chat converts content blocks (strips thinking/redacted_thinking/image/cache_control, transforms tool_use to tool_calls with dict-validated input and NaN/non-dict to placeholder degradation, tool_result to role:tool paired by tool_use_id, user text blocks joined to string, empty user messages dropped, assistant text preserved as separate message when tool_calls present, non-dict blocks traced, tool_use id/name guarded), _transform_anthropic_tools_to_chat converts input_schema to parameters with cache_control stripping, and _transform_anthropic_tool_choice_to_chat maps Anthropic tool_choice to OpenAI equivalents. _anthropic_to_chat was rewired to call all three transforms, building output without mutating input. Three trace events added: content_block_dropped (coalesced per-request with dropped_counts including tool_result), cache_control_stripped (once per request with locations list via cache_stripped_out out-parameter), and tool_args_parse_failure (on NaN/non-dict input). A Phase 6 review found 3 Warnings and 6 Suggestions, all resolved. 151 tests pass across 3 rounds. Confirmed working against live opencode-go provider. Two issues deferred: streaming tool call deltas and image content blocks.

Threaded request_id, mode, and provider through the response transform call chain (_transform_and_guard to _chat_to_anthropic and _response_to_anthropic), replacing 13 hardcoded request_id None trace events with fully correlated fields. Replaced the tool_use with input empty-dict fallback with a user-visible text block error message (Option C extended) for JSONDecodeError, non-dict parse results, empty dicts, non-dict function values, and non-dict tool-call entries. Added emitted_tool_use flag inside the isinstance tool_calls list block with stop_reason degradation mirroring the SSE path. Fixed null tool_calls plus finish_reason tool_calls producing stop_reason tool_use with zero blocks (client hang). Isolated the test suite from the live proxy state file via PROXY_STATE_FILE env-var override in cli.py and server.py, with a module-scope os.environ override in test_claude_proxy.py. All 123 tests pass with the live proxy up. Two mega-audit iterations (34 and 39 findings). Files: server.py, cli.py, test_claude_proxy.py, CLAUDE.md, README.md.

Added three endpoint modes to the multi-provider retry gateway: anthropic (Anthropic Messages API, existing behavior), chat (OpenAI Chat Completions), and response (OpenAI Responses). Each vendor entry in keys-index.json may carry an optional mode field defaulting to anthropic. Mode dispatch controls auth header (x-api-key vs Authorization: Bearer), upstream path construction (original path vs /v1/chat/completions vs /v1/responses with trailing-/v1 stripping), request body transformation (model-only rewrite vs full Anthropic-to-Chat vs Anthropic-to-Responses), and response body transformation (model-only rewrite vs Chat-to-Anthropic vs Responses-to-Anthropic). Chat-mode SSE streaming synthesizes Anthropic SSE events from OpenAI SSE with frame assembly on double-newline delimiters, synthetic message_start/content_block_start/content_block_delta/content_block_stop/message_delta/message_stop events, and terminal synthesis on EOF. Response mode forces stream false and is single-turn only. Two Critical review findings were fixed: SSE events now carry the required event line for Anthropic SDK dispatch, and tool_calls delta tracking degrades stop_reason to null when tool calls are seen but not transformed. Admin page shows mode per provider via GET /admin/api/providers-detail. All error responses pass through untransformed. 121 tests pass (53 new mode-dispatch tests, 68 pre-existing tests unaffected).

Two bug fixes from the recently completed dynamic-providers-no-collision plan. Fix 1 reversed the validate_config direction from keys-to-config to config-to-keys: the old check iterated all providers in keys-index.json and required each to have models in config.models, but keys-index.json is a credential store that may contain inactive or legacy providers. The new checks validate that every provider in config.models has a valid shape (non-empty list of non-empty strings), that every provider in config.models has a corresponding entry in keys-index.json (config-to-keys), and that every provider referenced by a tier has an entry in config.models (tiers-to-models). Providers in keys-index.json that are not in config.models and not referenced by any tier are silently ignored. Fix 2 addressed a heartbeat state corruption bug where the heartbeat_loop read state from disk, modified last_heartbeat, and wrote back; if the CLI cleanup deleted the state file during a failed start attempt, read_state returned an empty dict and the heartbeat wrote a degraded state file with only last_heartbeat, losing the pid and port fields permanently. The fix stores the server startup state in a module-level _startup_state variable at init and the heartbeat writes from that in-memory copy, never reading from disk. If the state file is deleted externally, the next heartbeat recreates it with all fields intact within 30 seconds. Three new permanent tests were added and one existing test was updated; 68 of 68 tests pass. CLAUDE.md and README.md were updated to document the new validation direction and heartbeat behavior.

This plan addressed two issues in the claude-retry-proxy gateway. First, newly added providers in keys-index.json had no model suggestions in the admin page because the models section in config.json had no entry for them. The fix cleaned up admin.html dropdowns to be strict select elements with no placeholder or custom options, populated solely from config.models, and added startup validation that every provider in keys-index.json must have at least one model in config.models with shape validation (must be a non-empty list of non-empty strings, rejecting bare strings, empty strings, and whitespace-only entries). Second, the proxy refused to start if two tiers mapped to the same model name due to a build_reverse_map collision check. The fix eliminated build_reverse_map and the _reverse_model_map global entirely, using the per-request tier variable (already threaded through the ThreadingHTTPServer call chain per thread) directly in _rewrite_sse_first_event and _rewrite_json_response instead of a reverse map lookup. The dead CSS selector select, input in admin.html was also fixed. The test suite was updated with test_models_per_provider_validation (including malformed entry cases) and test_two_tiers_same_model_same_provider, and test_config_validation_reverse_map_collision was removed. CLAUDE.md and README.md were updated to reflect the changes. All 65 tests pass across 5 modified files.

Three-part plan covering Windows readiness probe fix, count_tokens retry control, and test suite completion. Part A fixed claude-retry-proxy start on Windows where select.select fails on pipe fds, replacing it with a thread-based READY detection via daemon thread reading proc.stdout lines (cross-platform, 5s timeout) followed by a TCP probe (2s timeout). Also fixed admin page model dropdown to use provider-keyed models instead of tier-keyed, reversed tier display order to opus-sonnet-haiku, fixed a missing _config_path global declaration in server.py, renamed admin buttons to Apply and Reload, and made the trace log model field record the actual upstream model name. Part B added a disable_retry_claude_count_token config flag (default true in shipped template) that skips retrying the count_tokens endpoint since third-party providers return 503/connection-errors for this Anthropic-specific endpoint, wasting retries and provider quota. The flag is validated as boolean in validate_config, preserved across admin hot-switches, and read from disk on reload. Retry log messages were enriched with model, provider, and request_id fields. Part C introduced plain unencrypted keys-index.json support: the server and CLI auto-detect the format by checking for VimCrypt~03! magic bytes at the start of the file, decrypting if encrypted or parsing as plain JSON otherwise with a stderr warning. This eliminated the passphrase requirement for testing. A new load_keys_file function replaced the old decrypt_keys flow, rejecting unsupported VimCrypt~01/02 prefixes. The CLI gained --passphrase-file for non-interactive encrypted-key starts. The tester implemented 18 new or rewritten permanent tests (4 CLI-start tests rewritten from old URL-swap-based bodies, 14 admin and CLI stub SKIPs implemented with real coverage), plus test infrastructure helpers for plain keys. Six dead old-CLI test functions referencing URL-swap, base-url.lock, and settings.json manipulation were deleted. CLAUDE.md and README.md were updated with plain keys file documentation including the vim -n -x recommendation, auto-detection description, Windows ACL note, and a JSON example. Full suite 64/64 PASS across 7 modified files (server.py, cli.py, admin.html, config-template.json, test_claude_proxy.py, CLAUDE.md, README.md). All 10 issues resolved.

Converted the retry proxy from a single-upstream proxy into a multi-provider HTTP gateway that routes Claude API requests by model tier (haiku/sonnet/opus) to different upstream providers simultaneously. Tier routing is configured via ~/.claude/proxy/config.json with a tiers table mapping each tier to a provider and model name, plus a models catalog for admin page dropdowns. Provider credentials are stored encrypted in ~/.claude/keys-index.json (vim blowfish2 format) and decrypted at startup via a passphrase pipe protocol (CLI writes passphrase to server stdin, server reads one line before serve_forever). Model names are rewritten bidirectionally: requests have tier names replaced with actual model names, responses have actual model names replaced with tier names (SSE streaming buffers the first event up to a 64KB cap to rewrite message_start, subsequent events stream in real-time). An admin HTML page at /admin/ provides hot-switching of tier mappings via a drain-and-swap pattern that blocks new queries during config swap, drains in-flight requests with a 30s timeout, swaps under lock, and unblocks. The forward_request method snapshots config, vendors, and reverse_map atomically under _config_lock to prevent mid-request config races. All admin POST endpoints (switch, reload, shutdown) validate CSRF via Origin header checking (reject missing, null, or non-localhost origins). The CLI was redesigned with start/stop/status/reload commands using a readiness handshake (server prints READY after binding, CLI waits up to 5s before TCP probe). A new PROXY_MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE env var (default 100MiB) caps streaming response size. Test suite grew from 36 to 51 tests covering tier routing, model resolution (direct, reverse lookup, pattern match), response rewriting (JSON and SSE), admin API, config validation, key decryption, and drain-and-swap. All 51 tests pass. Reviewer found 2 non-blocking warnings (drain-swap race fixed with atomic snapshot, cmd_stop CSRF fixed with Origin header) and 1 documentation suggestion (PROXY_MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE documented in both CLAUDE.md and README.md).

The proxy buffered entire upstream response bodies before writing anything to the client, so long streaming generations (Claude API with stream true) produced zero bytes for the whole generation duration, causing Claude Code's HTTP client to time out with Connection lost mid-response. The plan converted the proxy to streaming delivery: on a non-retryable 2xx response the new _stream_upstream_response method sends the status line and filtered headers immediately, then copies the body in read1(8192) chunks written and flushed to the client as they arrive, while non-2xx responses stay on the buffered path so upstream error bodies remain available for the trace log. Retries never happen after the first byte reaches the client: mid-stream upstream truncation aborts the stream (dual-path detection — IncompleteRead on chunked bodies, clean EOF on close-delimited), and client-side write errors are caught by an outer _DISCONNECT_ERRORS handler that logs a client_disconnect event and returns without re-raising. The originally prescribed resp.read(8192) proved unable to stream — http.client read(amt) fills amt bytes or EOF before returning, caught by the tester as a blocking Plan Error — and the loop was revised to resp.read1(8192), verified empirically to deliver per-arrival on both close-delimited and chunked upstreams (first byte 22ms while the upstream is still generating). Step 5 added a module-level _crlf_safe helper that skips any response header whose name or value contains CR or LF, applied to both the streaming path and _send_response as a parser-differential response-splitting guard; streamed success bodies are no longer captured under PROXY_LOG_ALL (deliberate data-at-rest reduction). The suite grew from 32 to 36 behavioral tests including real-time first-byte timing, dual-mode mid-stream truncation, empty-body 429 exhaustion, and the CRLF unit test; the Phase 6 review gate passed with 0 Critical findings and 2 acknowledged non-blocking Warnings (truncated streams traced as success; non-disconnect client-write OSErrors can reach the retry loop).

Three behavior fixes surfaced by inspecting the live proxy trace log and stderr. Fix B: forward_request on retry exhaustion (429/503 or connection error) now preserves the upstream error body instead of returning b''. The final-attempt drain is capped at PROXY_MAX_BODY_SIZE via a new _read_capped helper that uses a truncated flag to distinguish exact-boundary from actual truncation, returning a standalone marker on real truncation. On connection-error exhaustion, a synthesized upstream_unreachable JSON body includes the sanitized last error string. Fix C: _send_response calls in do_POST are wrapped in try/except _DISCONNECT_ERRORS (ConnectionResetError, BrokenPipeError, ConnectionAbortedError); on disconnect a client_disconnect trace event is logged instead of a per-request traceback. The _log_client_disconnect method wraps its own log_trace call in try/except to prevent re-raise. Fix D: cmd_start now checks and prunes the trace log before spawning the server, removing entries older than 5 days (hardcoded). The prune streams line-by-line to a temp file using json.loads per line for reliable extraction even with PROXY_LOG_ALL, counts malformed lines in kept_count, and is wrapped in try/except as a best-effort operation that does not block startup. Five new permanent tests were added covering body preservation, synthesized connection-error body, client disconnect handling, trace pruning, and edge cases. Design decisions were validated through two mega-audit iterations: iteration 1 overturned the initial no cap decision on the give-up drain (final-attempt resp is fresh and unread, so resp.read() is an unbounded allocation), added ConnectionAbortedError to the disconnect tuple, and required streaming the prune rather than reading the full file into memory; iteration 2 corrected the truncation marker to a standalone return rather than appended concatenated JSON. Test count went from 27 to 32.

Added ±25% uniform jitter to the retry backoff and extended retries to cover HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) in addition to the existing 503 and connection-error handling. The jitter uses a per-thread random.Random() instance (thread-local, not the module-global Mersenne Twister which is unsafe under ThreadingHTTPServer worker threads) and applies math.floor(base + jitter + 0.5) for unbiased half-up integer rounding, avoiding Python 3 banker's rounding which collapses small even bases. The 429 path uses PROXY_MAX_DELAY directly (maximal latency) while the 503 path keeps the existing exponential backoff capped at PROXY_MAX_DELAY, both then jittered. The status check in forward_request was merged into a defensive if 429 / elif 503 / else dispatch with resp.read() draining the response body before conn.close() on retry paths. Exhaustion returns the actual upstream status (429 stays 429, not 503). Three new permanent tests were added: compute_jittered_delay_bounds (33 assertions covering bounds, rounding, de-sync pattern, guard clauses, thread-local RNG), retry_429 (mock upstream returns 429 then 200), and retry_429_exhaust_returns_429. All tests pass (9/9). An honest caveat: integer-second rounding means ±25% jitter is degenerate for base in {1, 2} (the ±0.5s range lands in one integer bucket), so de-sync is only effective from base >= 3. On the 503 path this means the 3rd retry onward; on the 429 path (using PROXY_MAX_DELAY default 30) it de-syncs from the first retry.

Extracted the Claude API retry proxy out of the personal claude-config repository into a standalone, public, pip-installable package named claude-retry-proxy. The proxy is a stdlib-only HTTP server (ThreadingHTTPServer on localhost) that forwards requests to the upstream ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL read from ~/.claude/settings.json, retries 503 responses with exponential backoff, and logs every request to a JSONL trace file; a CLI manager (start/stop/status) swaps the base URL in settings.json to localhost while the proxy runs and restores it on stop, with lock-file crash recovery and cross-platform PID liveness and kill via ctypes on Windows. Key decisions: hardcoded ~/.claude/settings.json as the sole URL store with no env-var fallback, package and console command both named claude-retry-proxy (renamed from claude-proxy), Python 3.8 plus setuptools 64 floor for PEP 660 src-layout editable installs, zero runtime dependencies, MIT license. The server's upstream-URL resolution was moved from import time into main() so direct invocation reads settings at runtime and emits a clean error; trace and state files get a POSIX-only 0o600 chmod (a near-no-op on Windows, documented). The 24-test suite was ported from claude-config with the non-portable deploy-protection test dropped, the test runner's prerequisite block rewritten to use importlib find_spec, SourceFileLoader replaced with direct imports, and dead auth-token plumbing removed with probe_ok readiness guards. Implementation is complete and tested at 23 of 24 passing; the sole failure is a pre-existing upstream Windows port-bind readiness race (the CLI TCP probe can report success on an occupied port) left as a documented future-work TODO alongside the response-streaming has no size cap issue.
